prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone—what’s best depends on your needs (whole-house vs one room, budget, timeline, prep/repairs required, desire for color consultation, etc.). I can, however, help you find the right contractor and point you to highly reputable options.

Quick next steps I recommend
- Tell me a few specifics so I can narrow recommendations: residential or commercial, whole house or a few rooms, any repair/trim/ceiling work, your ZIP code or neighborhood, and your target budget/timeline.
- If you want, I can produce a short list of highly rated painters near you (you’ll need to give me your ZIP or neighborhood).

How to choose the best painter for your project
1. Read recent reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor) and look for repeat positives about punctuality, cleanup, and accuracy to estimate.
2. Verify insurance and, if required, business license. Ask for proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
3. Ask for at least three written, line-item estimates (paint brand/finish, # coats, prep work, timelines).
4. Check references and photos of finished projects similar to yours.
5. Confirm warranty/guarantee on workmanship and paint.
6. Ask about prep: will they fill cracks, sand, prime? Inadequate prep causes problems later.
7. Discuss paint brands (Benjamin Moore, Sherwin-Williams, etc.) and specific finishes.
8. Get payment terms in writing (deposit amount, milestone payments, final inspection).

Questions to ask a painter when getting estimates
- How many coats of paint do you include?
- Do you prime or spot-prime? Is primer included in the estimate?
- How will you protect floors and furniture? How do you handle cleanup?
- What is your projected start and completion date?
- Can you provide proof of insurance and three local references?
- Do you offer a warranty? What does it cover?

Typical cost guidance (very approximate)
- One room (average 10x12): $300–$1,000 depending on prep and quality of paint.
- Whole interior: $2,000–$10,000+ depending on size and level of prep/trim work.
- Cost drivers: amount of prep/repair, number of coats, trim/ceiling work, high ceilings, and premium paints.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial and I’ll list top-rated painters in the St. Louis area and a suggested short checklist tailored to those companies.
